Let \(n\) be the number of participants. The \(n-2\) eliminated players each have exactly 2 losses, so they account for \(2(n-2)\) losses.

The two remaining players have at most 1 loss each, so total losses \(29\) satisfy:
\[
2(n-2) \le 29 \le 2(n-2)+2
\]
\[
2n-4 \le 29 \le 2n-2
\]
\[
31 \le 2n \le 33
\]
Thus \(n=16\).

\boxed{16}
